mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which correlates with lower earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.5% over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which typically precedes recession and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases while CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in HOUST above its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals rising housing demand, which correlates with stronger consumer confidence and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS above 0.4% month-over-month and a fall in UNRATE below 3.5% signals a softening labor market with stable employment, which typically supports corporate margins and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening retail sales, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered periods.
